_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC §4
protagonist: Amara Osei, harbor pilot, Port of Kesterhaven Pilots' Association

deliverables.text: A worked angle table for each key clock time across the transit window: the time converted to the tide model's angle in degrees and radians, the reference angle, and the sine, cosine, and tangent of that reference angle, found using the unit circle.
A stated sine or cosine function modeling the tide station's predicted water level over the transit window, naming its amplitude and period, fitted to the real harmonic data in Appendix A.
An under-keel clearance table comparing the Dawn Transit and the Slack Tide, in feet, built by evaluating the D2 model at the times from D1.

A written sensitivity check: using the barometric/storm-surge range in Appendix D, show whether the Dawn Transit's clearance margin survives the worst case in that range, and state the assumption used to model it.

balance.argument_a: The tide model predicts a real, positive under-keel clearance at the marginal low -- 4.824 ft, a 1.544 ft (about 47%) buffer over the Pilots' Association's 3.28 ft minimum-clearance policy, computed directly from Appendix A/B's real sourced figures under MA4's stated governing-depth convention (54 ft entrance channel). Holding for the Slack Tide guarantees the MA2 late-delivery penalty, a real and immediate cost with no offsetting benefit if the predicted clearance holds.
balance.argument_b: Under MA3's stated storm assumption (a real, documented wind-driven setdown, well within the range such events actually reach, not a landfalling hurricane's storm surge), the Dawn Transit's margin over policy erodes from 1.544 ft to 0.634 ft -- a real ~59% reduction, though it does NOT flip the clearance negative under this specific stated assumption. The Pilots' Association's policy exists precisely because a margin that shrinks by more than half on one plausible weather event is not the same as a margin that was never real. The penalty for missing the window is a known, bounded cost; a margin call that turns out wrong is not. Separately, MA4's governing-depth convention is itself a live fault line: under the alternate, equally sourced 52 ft inner-harbor reading, Option A's margin is already negative before any storm is modeled at all.
balance.margin_basis: RESOLVED 2026-08-05 (was null; see qa.note for full history). This is a threshold comparison (clearance vs. a policy floor), not a two-option ratio the way Cold Chain's dose count was -- comparing Option A's clearance margin directly to Option B's is not meaningful (B is a high-tide transit and will always clear by several times more than A's marginal-low transit; that gap is a structural fact of the two options, not a close call, and no real constraint can honestly close it without misrepresenting Appendix A/B's sourced NOAA/vessel data). The graded margin_pct instead measures how close Option A's real safety margin comes to the policy floor under MA3's stress-test twist (the only genuinely adjustable, disclosed-as-uncertain quantity in this case -- MA1/MA2 affect only the schedule/dollar side, and S1-S8 are real sourced facts, not free parameters). MA3's pressure-drop assumption was retuned from 20 mb (originally 'the middle' of the real 13-33 mb tropical-storm range) to 28 mb (toward the upper end of that same real, cited range, per SPEC section 2's 'retune a constraint, not hide data') -- still a genuine, disclosed, non-landfalling tropical-storm-strength assumption, not a fabricated one. Under that stress test, Option A's margin over the 3.28 ft policy floor is 0.634 ft, i.e. 19.33% of the floor -- inside SPEC's ~20% cap. See derived{} for the full worked arithmetic.
balance.stability: FIXED 2026-08-17 -- the 2026-08-12 note this replaces described a real bug as a 'known script/case-shape mismatch' rather than fixing it: sensitivity_model.py's evaluate() computed the PRE-twist figure (47.07%) while case.json's own graded margin_pct is the POST-twist figure (19.33%), so probe 5's mechanical sweep of setdown_ft (MA3's headline assumption) against evaluate() had literally zero effect on the metric it claimed to be testing -- evaluate() hardcoded setdown_ft=0. evaluate()/evaluate_twist() are now swapped so evaluate() IS the case's real graded primary_metric (post-twist, matches case.json.derived and margin_pct exactly: A=3.914, B=3.28, margin_pct=19.33%); evaluate_twist() now returns the pre-twist predicted baseline as a disclosed, non-graded context metric only. Re-run (tier2_probes.py --probe 5, 2026-08-17): mechanically FAIL, but correctly so and for a real reason -- flexing setdown_ft -50% (to 0.455 ft) does not flip the verdict (A still clears the floor) but pushes margin_pct to 33.2%, over the SPEC section 2 20% cap; +50% (1.365 ft) stays under the cap at 5.5%. This is disclosed, not hidden: see sensitivity_disclosure[] (param setdown_ft, category F -- a genuine forecast/irreducible-unknown dial per Appendix D's own 'not knowable in advance' language), which the disclosure-aware pass state (skills/case-readiness, 2026-08-13) allows to PASS (disclosed) rather than forcing a fake retune. late_penalty_usd (MA2) still moves neither A nor B under either function -- expected, MA2 is a schedule/dollar dial, not a safety dial. MA4 (not FLEXed, a discrete either/or) is unchanged: the alternate 52 ft governing-depth reading flips Option A to PROHIBITED pre-twist, standalone -- see modeling_assumptions MA4 and derived.alt_ma4_52ft_pretwist_margin_over_policy_ft.

cohort_bands.note: Socratic plan and anchor timings run as written in FACILITATOR.md (0:00-45:00). Anchor 1 vote is a real show-of-hands split worth reading; all three deep-conflict threads run.

Anchors 2 and 3 combine into one pass ('what are we solving, and how'). Run only one deep-conflict thread (prediction vs. policy — it needs the least setup) at 20:00-30:00. Twist still drops at 15:00. Total runtime ~30 min.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: The Dawn Transit meets it; the Slack Tide misses it, triggering MA2's penalty
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public source states a specific fictional charter's delivery window terms -- this cannot exist publicly by construction. The case only needs the qualitative fact that the Slack Tide option misses the window.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Does not flip the dilemma on its own.

modeling_assumptions.value_used: $18,000 flat penalty for missing the contracted window
modeling_assumptions.basis: Real container demurrage runs $75-$300 per container per day; a real worked charter-party example runs $20,000/day (see RESEARCH_LOG.md P09/P10). $18,000 is set as roughly one day's worth of that real charter-rate example, treated as a flat incident cost rather than a per-day accrual since the case does not model how many days the Slack Tide actually delays the ship. This fictional charter's exact clause cannot exist publicly, but the order of magnitude is grounded in real industry figures, not guessed from nothing.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing on Argument A. If set materially lower, Option B (Slack Tide, always safe) dominates outright and the case stops being close; if set materially higher, Option A dominates. case-qa/Tier 2 probe 5 should flex this +/-50% (MCS-26) once a sensitivity_model.py exists for this case.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Local water-level reduction modeled for the Twist's offshore storm
modeling_assumptions.basis: CORRECTED 2026-08-12: earlier drafts derived this figure as '28 mb local pressure drop -> 0.91 ft water-level reduction via S8's rate' -- but S8's inverse-barometer rate produces a RISE for a pressure drop (that is the real physics of ordinary storm surge), not a reduction, so it could not honestly justify this row's sign. Found by an adversarial Tier 2 twist-integrity probe (P4) and independently verified directly against case.md's own Appendix D/E text before this fix. The real mechanism is wind-driven setdown ('reverse storm surge') -- a separate, real, opposite-signed effect where a storm's offshore wind physically pushes water away from the coast (S10), consistent with this case's own 'offshore, non-landfalling system' framing. Real documented setdowns reach ~4 ft (Tampa Bay, Hurricane Ian, 2022 -- S10); this case's 0.91 ft is a genuine but non-extreme fraction of that real range, not picked to force an outcome. S9's tropical-storm-strength context (980-1000+ mb) is retained as scene-setting for how strong a storm this case models, but is no longer the numeric basis for the ft figure.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Computed result (see case.json.derived): reduces the Dawn Transit's margin over the Pilots' Association policy from +1.544 ft to +0.634 ft (19.33% of the 3.28 ft policy floor) -- a real ~59% erosion, but it does NOT flip the clearance negative under this specific value. A materially larger setdown (~1.54 ft, roughly 40% of Tampa Bay's real documented ~4 ft) would zero the margin -- close enough to a real documented event that a guide could legitimately ask 'what if the wind had been stronger' as a live follow-on question. See cases/tide-window/sensitivity_model.py for the mechanical +/-50% flex (does not flip the verdict) and RESEARCH_LOG.md for the correction.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Governing charted depth for the Dawn Transit's clearance calculation
modeling_assumptions.basis: ADDED 2026-08-12 to fix a real defect: Appendix B cites two real, both-sourced, dated depths for this harbor -- 54 ft entrance channel and 52 ft inner harbor (S6) -- without stating which one governs this fictional vessel's specific route, which is not itself a matter of public record. Earlier drafts silently used 54 ft in case.json.derived without disclosing this as a choice, found as a BLOCKER by an adversarial Tier 2 twist-integrity probe (P4): a student reading Appendix B literally could equally defensibly apply 52 ft instead. This case models the Dawn Transit's controlling clearance moment as occurring at the harbor entrance itself, the transit's final and most exposed segment on the way to open water, and the general area the real NOAA tide station behind Appendix A's predictions is sited in.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: This is the single largest lever in the whole case, larger than MA2 or MA3. Under the alternate, equally natural 52 ft reading, the Dawn Transit's PRE-TWIST margin over the policy floor is already negative (-0.456 ft) -- Option A would fail the safety floor before any storm is even modeled, which would collapse the entire dilemma as currently framed. Not swept by the +/-50% FLEX convention (it is a disclosed convention about which real, sourced figure applies, not an authored scenario magnitude) -- see cases/tide-window/sensitivity_model.py's __main__ block for the discrete 52 ft check, and FACILITATOR.md for how to handle a Hero who raises it.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: ADDED 2026-08-17 after fixing sensitivity_model.py's evaluate()/evaluate_twist() mismatch (see that file's module docstring): flexing MA3's setdown_ft -50% (to 0.455 ft) against the case's real GRADED post-twist margin does not flip the verdict (A still clears the floor) but pushes margin_pct to 33.2%, over the SPEC section 2 20% cap. This is a genuine forecast/irreducible-unknown dial, not a modeling error: Appendix D states outright that 'the specific magnitude is not knowable in advance' for an offshore, non-landfalling storm's wind-driven setdown on this specific night, and the case's own MA3 text says the same. The +50% direction (1.365 ft) stays under the cap at 5.5%. No retune was applied because 0.91 ft is already a real, disclosed, non-extreme choice within S10's documented range; narrowing it further to force P5 stability would misrepresent how uncertain a real storm forecast actually is.
